correctness.rationale: For one P8, selecting three nonadjacent edges among seven yields exactly ten edge sets. A direct trace calculation finds a shattered pair but no shattered triple, so VC=2; an independent recursive version-space game finds Ldim=3, with ten hypotheses ruling out depth four. For all paths of at most six edges, an exhaustive exact all-ranks check finds no Ldim >=3. For product classes on disjoint ground sets, VC and Littlestone dimensions add: a shattered set restricts to shattered sets in each coordinate, and adaptive trees can be combined; for the upper bound on sequential depth the standard finite game rank has additivity under product of independent label domains. Thus disjoint s-fold products have 2s and 3s, with precise per-component quotas. Independently reconstructed every source tree and tested the finite base/marginal path cases. No claim about a *single global* fixed quota across components or arbitrary graphs.

value.rationale: The exact disparity on a natural finite combinatorial family demonstrates a structural separation of static and adaptive prediction for *fixed-rank matchings*, with the smallest possible path size for adaptive depth three and a parametrized sequence whose gap grows linearly. The product extension is elementary, but the minimal graph-constrained witness and its full static/adaptive certificate are motivated by complexity of learning matching hypotheses, not an arbitrary unmotivated slice. The result does not claim a new general VC/Littlestone inequality.
